answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to periodically demonstrate exclusive control of a distinct physical token carved from cedar wood and embedded with a jade-grade secure element that must be physically presented at a rotating harbor checkpoint for live attestation. Because the token is non-transferable without destruction and the harbor visit cannot be virtualized, an attacker must purchase and transport a separate cedar-jade device for every fake identity on every epoch, imposing a hard linear hardware-plus-logistics cost that cannot be amortized.
